alignments.note: Rule 23: the ASV supplies no nominal for the article to take — *our* is ἡμῶν's, *light* is ἐλαφρόν's, *affliction* is θλίψεως' — so nothing is left for it. PHP.4.5 τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν -> *your forbearance* is the unhedged structural twin: substantival article over an adjective, free genitive pronoun, no supplied nominal, unrepresented. Rule 49's τὸ τρίτον -> *the third part* does not reach it, because there the ASV supplied *part* and wrote *of them* rather than a possessive. Medium is for the rule 31 reading, which would give the article the supplied *which* — the same seam the παραυτίκα unit concedes.
Displaced by the possessive 'our' realizing the genitive hemon (rule 20).

The adverb is expanded into a supplied finite relative clause *which is for the moment*; with no verb and no preposition in the Greek, the adverb carries the relativizer, copula and determiner as rule 7 helpers, headed on *moment* as its own gloss (rules 53, 91). Giving *which* to the article under rule 31 remains defensible, and the corpus does put a bare *which is* on an attributive article in 4 of its 5 such units (REV.10.8, REV.11.2, REV.14.17, REV.9.13); that is the one seam this medium and s001's are both paying for.

Rule 2 splits the phrase and rule 34 empties the preposition: no English word answers to καθ᾽ separately, and GAL.1.13 splits this very phrase καθ᾽ ὑπερβολήν. The pair was one aligned unit, but every aligned PREP+X unit in the corpus renders to exactly one English word, so an aligned compound spanning *and more exceedingly* had no precedent anywhere; splitting both phrases keeps them symmetric. Medium: reading all four tokens as one noncompositional unit on *more and more exceedingly* remains defensible (JHN.19.18 is that shape), though rule 6 reserves that status for the genuinely indivisible and the ASV's *more … and more* tracks the Greek doubling. The corpus is divided on a κατά phrase English realizes nowhere: 2CO.11.28 καθ᾽ ἡμέραν -> *daily* is noncompositional, also medium and also conceding.

ὑπερβολήν takes the first *more* of the distributive *more and more exceedingly*. Rule 91 cannot decide the head between *more* and *exceedingly*, the corpus spending neither on this lexeme, which is the second reason for medium.
Rule 34: no English word answers to εἰς separately. Split as s008 above.
The second ὑπερβολήν takes *and more exceedingly*, the juncture *and* being an obligatory helper on what it introduces (rule 29); headed on *exceedingly*. Same seam and same confidence as s009.
The case preposition *for* rides with the pronoun (rule 21). Rule 36 governs an expressed Greek preposition and there is none here.
Both adjective and noun are anarthrous, so the supplied determiner belongs to the noun (rule 58), discontinuously under rule 15.
